judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit under the same Grade 1, Term 4, Reading and Phonics / 'Daily Phonic Activities of 15 minutes' sub-strand (same rank 1, same term), so shared placement alone is not decisive. The pair-specific evidence is substantive: the second SFI is explicit phonic manipulation — using consonant blends to build up (blend) and break down (segment) words (sp-o-t, fr-o-g, dr-i-nk, st-i-ck), with LCs tagged blending/segmenting/building words; the first SFI requires spelling ten words a week 'taken from phonics lessons', i.e. encoding exactly the blend-based words taught in those lessons. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each) and both carry upstream audit/merge context, so the judgment rests on the bounded statement text, LCs and shared Term 4 phonics table row.

judgment.rationale: Both SFIs are Grade 3 (rank 3) Skills about the same punctuation set (full stops, question marks, exclamation marks, inverted commas), but they differ substantively in modality and demand. The first sits in Grade 3 Term 1, Reading and Phonics / Group Guided Reading, and requires receptive recognition and interpretation of punctuation while reading aloud. The second sits in Grade 3 Term 2, Writing / Shared, Group and Independent Writing, and requires productive, correct use of punctuation in the learner's own writing, extended to capital letters and commas. Direction is from the earlier Term 1 reading-aloud skill to the later Term 2 writing skill, consistent with the within-grade term ordering; recognising what punctuation signals in text plausibly supports success in applying it accurately when composing. judgment.rationale: Both SFIs are Grade 2 (rank 2), Term 1, Skill Area 'Reading and Phonics', but sit under different printed sub-strands: the second under 'Daily Phonic Activities of 15 minutes:' (Phonics) and the first under 'Group Guided Reading'. The second statement ('Builds 3 and 4-letter words using the single letters and digraphs taught this term'; LC tags digraphs, phonics, spelling, word building) is explicit letter/digraph-level word construction, while the first ('Uses sight words, phonics, contextual and structural analysis decoding skills when reading'; LC tags decoding, phonics, reading, sight words) applies phonic knowledge plus contextual/structural analysis to decode during guided reading of connected text. Proficiency in building words from the taught single letters and digraphs plausibly supports success in applying phonics as one of several decoding strategies while reading, a substantive extension from isolated word building to integrated in-text decoding rather than generic repeated wording (shared tokens are only 'and'/'words'/'phonics'). Direction is within the same Grade and same Term, so earlier-to-same-term is permitted. Both endpoints have truncated source evidence (24 omitted items each) and carry upstream audit/merge context, which limits certainty, hence moderate confidence.
